question.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $z,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

Using the chain rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{4y-x{z}^{4}}) \\  & ={e}^{4y-x{z}^{4}}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂z}(4y-x{z}^{4})\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the sum and constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{4y-x{z}^{4}}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂z}(4y-x{z}^{4}) & ={e}^{4y-x{z}^{4}}\cdot (\frac{∂}{∂z}(4y)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(x{z}^{4})) \\  & ={e}^{4y-x{z}^{4}}\cdot (0-x\frac{∂}{∂z}({z}^{4})) \\  & =-{e}^{4y-x{z}^{4}}\cdot x\cdot 4{z}^{3} \\  & =-4x{z}^{3}{e}^{4y-x{z}^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂z}=-4x{z}^{3}{e}^{4y-x{z}^{4}}.
$$
